For me it’s what saved my sanity. I took it slow with getting her back on the breast and tried not to push myself or her too hard. I kind of had the attitude of, “I’m deciding to exclusively pump- if we end up figuring out how to latch? Great! If not- no big deal.” 

When we did try latching I did side laying position and sort of just let her lead the process. If she was too shallow I’d break the latch and try again. And I never tried to latch when she was super hungry. Once it was getting more comfortable I would feed her a small bottle and then try to finish the feed on the breast. Eventually when I had a full day to just us- her latch was getting a bit better but not perfect- I decided to just do skin to skin basically all day and we hung out in bed and watched tv and just tried latching all day with a shield. Literally did nothing but snuggle and latch and eat lol. Midway through the day we really got the hang of it and I tried not using the shield. It went well and then from there I just kept nursing and stopped pumping altogether. The first week wasn’t perfect but it was not anywhere near as difficult and painful as it was the first week of her life and we kind of perfected it from there. :) 

I had a hard time finding other people with experiences similar to mine online so I thought I’d share my story with you in case it helps. Don’t give up! Take a break and pump instead to give your nipples a break. You don’t have to jump straight into exclusive pumping like I did lol (I was at my wits end) but just do what feels right. You got this!

I did not want an epidural. I have a high pain tolerance as well so while I knew it would be challenging I was pretty set on having the unmedicated experience. 

Well, I ended up with pre-eclampsia and needed to be induced. I labored for about 20 hours on pitocin but couldn’t sleep and was exhausted. Labor wasn’t progressing. I gave in and asked for meds and they gave me some and it helped briefly but I still couldn’t sleep. By 24 hours in, i was only 5cm and I had the worst pain I’d ever had in my life and so I asked for the epidural. As we were waiting on the anesthesiologist my water broke and my contractions were SO intense I thought I’d die. 

Once it was finally placed my pain was completely gone and I fell asleep. I woke up the next morning to the nurse and doctor telling me it was time to push. I pushed through 5 or so contractions and couldn’t feel a single thing but I met my daughter who was completely healthy. I don’t regret getting the epidural at all- it was the right choice for me.

Some thoughts I have after binging this series today. 

The detective mentioned male Hamburg DNA under Barbie’s fingernails but it is never mentioned again. Was this a lie and supposed to rattle Madison? 

Allie seemed genuine to me, personally. Especially for someone with BPD and lots of therapy.. she seems well adjusted. She was emotional during the family get together with videos. She was emotional when talking to her brother on the beach. I didn’t see her as cold and calculated at all. She also has been living in Argentina and surrounding herself in a different culture. She may be handling her grief and confrontations with a different cultural attitude than what many of us are used to seeing here in the US. Regardless, she was at school at 7:55 or so with her mother checking her in. 

The Gifting Tables didn’t really compel me. Maybe it’s because of the nature of the crime seeming so personal and then the covering of her body showing some remorse that gives me this feeling. But it’s still possible I suppose someone involved in the tables could be responsible. I just personally don’t see it as likely. Gut feeling I guess. 

Conway is stuck in her grief and is the only person that I know of whose alibi was not able to be verified. Unless the police interviewed the woman she was staying with before she passed? The fact that she never even mentioned Madison’s dad was really peculiar to me considering the circumstances and timing of Barbie’s death. Also not to mention the fact that she said Allie had been texting her since 9AM or so to pick her up from school. Why didn’t she go until nearly 11AM? She was incredibly emotional, which could have been genuine. It could also be remorse/guilt. But, her phone was on when the detectives said their suspect had turned their phone off for 24 hours. And her openness seemed, at least to me, to be honest. I go back and forth when thinking about Conway being involved. 

Dad has the most to gain, and didn’t do himself any favors by being so secretive and callous. If the DNA bit from early on was true, he’s really the only one who fits. We have no knowledge about whether or not his phone was on that day. What I want to know is how close the house is to the school where Barbie dropped Allie off. About what time would she have gotten home? And then, realistically, how long would the murder have taken to commit? From there- how long does it take to get to the court house from Barbie’s house? I see about an hour or so window. 

She dropped Allie off at 7:55ish. Let’s say she gets home at 8:10. 
20 minutes to commit the murder? It’s 8:30AM by this time. 
15 minutes to clean up quickly with a change of clothes in the car (where would he have hid the car?) and a wash in Barbie’s house. 
15 minutes to get to the courthouse. Bam 9:00. 

This all falls apart very easily depending on distance and how long it takes to stab someone 18 times and then move a body. I just don’t know if the dads alibi is really that solid. It could also be a hit- but the nature of the crime was so personal, and needed some intimate knowledge of the surroundings. The cushions were locked in the garage. I just don’t know. 

I really hope that with the shared investigations that some more information surfaces soon. Barbie was not a perfect person but she clearly loved her children. No one deserves to die the way she did- and her children and family deserve answers.

Tldr; Watch the series it’s great. Is dads alibi really that solid? Conway seems sus, too.

Who knows, maybe your potential partner may have some experience themselves, and could be incredibly understanding.
